title: Detecting quantum phase transitions via shallow variational quantum circuits
abstract: Mapping quantum phase diagrams through classical simulation is notoriously resource-intensive, as even small systems far from the thermodynamic limit demand prohibitive computational effort. The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) offers a compelling alternative, exploiting approximate ground states to distinguish phases. An appealing proposal, dubbed as Delta-VQE, determines critical points by contrasting variational energies optimized from reference states of distinct phases. Intriguingly, the diagnostic sharpens as circuit depth decreases, highlighting its promise as a resource-conscious probe of quantum criticality. To probe the broader applicability and underlying mechanisms of this approach, we investigate the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model with a three-spin cluster interaction, a setting in which the Ising transitions are generally situated beyond the self-dual line. We demonstrate that, whenever dual ansätze are employed, Delta-VQE invariably detects the self-dual points rather than the true criticality. In contrast, when ansätze are carefully tailored to embody the competing phases across the boundary, the genuine Ising critical point can be successfully identified with only minor finite-size effects. Our results establish that, while Delta-VQE provides a resource-efficient probe of quantum criticality without requiring precise ground-state preparation, its diagnostic power is fundamentally contingent upon the judicious selection of physically representative ansätze.
summary: The paper introduces Delta-VQE, a variational quantum circuit technique designed to locate quantum phase transitions by measuring the energy difference between two distinct reference states. While resource-efficient, its accuracy hinges on selecting ansätze that physically represent the competing phases across the critical boundary, as general choices can lead to false positives at symmetry points.
main_problem: Detecting quantum phase transitions (QPTs) is computationally demanding using classical simulations, even for small systems.
main_result: The proposed Delta-VQE method can resource-efficiently probe QPTs, but its success critically depends on designing physically representative variational ansätze that correctly capture the competing phases across the transition boundary.
method: Delta-VQE determines critical points by calculating and minimizing the absolute energy difference ($\Delta E$) between two variational quantum circuits optimized from reference states corresponding to distinct phases. This contrasts with standard methods like fidelity susceptibility.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model with a three-spin cluster interaction, exhibiting various phases including Paramagnetic (PM), Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) cluster, Ferromagnetic (FM), and Antiferromagnetic (AFM).
key_observables: The primary diagnostic is $\Delta E = |E_1 - E_2|$, the absolute difference in variational energies. Other observables include order parameters and fidelity susceptibility ($\chi_F$).
important_parameters: Transverse field strength ($h$) and coupling constants ($J$), which define the phase diagram and critical points ($h_c$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the minimum of $\Delta E$ signals a quantum critical point. A major limitation is that using general dual ansätze can incorrectly identify self-dual points rather than true QCPs.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams, showing Ising transition lines and self-dual lines. They compare $\Delta E(h)$ results against fidelity susceptibility ($\chi_F$), demonstrating that $\Delta$-VQE shows less finite-size dependence when correctly implemented.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the resource challenge of QPT detection, details the Delta-VQE protocol using two variational ansätze for a cluster-Ising model, and then presents comparative results showing its efficacy versus fidelity susceptibility analysis under varying coupling strengths ($J$).
why_interesting: This work provides a quantum algorithm approach to characterizing phase transitions in strongly correlated systems, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent phenomena in condensed matter physics.
